evals.prompt: set up break-glass access to prod for on-call incidents
evals.expected_output: Designs break-glass as an explicit-invocation, auto-expiring path (minutes to hours) rather than a standing door, with every use logged with a reason and a mandatory post-use review, distinct from indefinite standing admin access.

evals.prompt: an auditor asked why priya still has prod db access from an incident 6 months ago
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses this as standing access that accumulated because it was granted individually rather than through a time-boxed role and never reviewed; fixes it by moving to role-based, short-lived grants and instituting a real quarterly access review cadence that actually revokes unused access, not just at offboarding.

evals.prompt: just give the new service an admin role for now, we'll scope it down later
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: 'scope it down later' rarely happens and standing broad access is a liability from day one; recommends granting through a narrowly defined, function-named role with least privilege and short-lived credentials instead of a static admin grant.
